title: 2014 AMC 12B 16
statement: Let \(P\) be a cubic polynomial with \(P(0) = k,\) \(P(1) = 2k,\) and \(P(-1) = 3k.\) What is \(P(2) + P(-2)?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(P(0) = k,\) write \(P(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + k.\)

Then \(P(1) = a+b+c+k = 2k\) and \(P(-1) = -a+b-c+k = 3k.\) Adding these gives \(2b + 2k = 5k,\) so \(2b = 3k.\)

The odd-power terms cancel in the sum: \[ \begin{gathered} P(2)+P(-2) \\ = (8a+4b+2c+k) \\ {}+ (-8a+4b-2c+k) \\ = 8b + 2k. \end{gathered} \] Since \(8b = 4(2b) = 12k,\) this equals \(12k + 2k = 14k.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write \(P(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + k\) using \(P(0)=k\)
